source_text: Ubi tunc Marcion, ponticus nauclerus, stoicae studiosus? Ubi Valentinus platonicae sectator? Nam constat illos, neque adeo olim fuisse, Antonini fere principatu, et in catholicae primo doctrinam credidisse apud Ecclesiam romanensem, sub episcopatu Eleutherii benedicti, donec ob inquietam semper eorum curiositatem, qua fratres quoque vitabant semel et iterum ejecti, Marcion quidem cum ducentis sestertiis quae Ecclesiae intulerat, novissime in perpetuum discidium relegati, venena doctrinarum suarum disseminaverunt. Postmodum idem Marcion, poenitentiam confessus cum conditioni datae sibi occurrit, ita pacem recepturus, si caeteros quos perditioni erudisset, Ecclesiae restitueret, morte praeventus est. Oportebat enim haereses esse. Nec tamen ideo bonum haereses, quia eas oportebat, quasi non et malum oportuerit esse. Nam et Dominum tradi oportebat; sed vae traditori? ne quis etiam hinc haereses defendat. Si et Apellis stemma retractandum est, tam non vetus et ipse quam Marcion institutor et praeformator ejus: sed lapsus in foeminam desertor continentiae marcionensis, ab oculis sanctissimi magistri Alexandriam secessit; inde post annos regressus non melior, nisi tantum qua jam non marcionites, in alteram foeminam impegit, illam virginem Philumenen, quam supra edidimus, postea vero immane prostibulum et ipsam, cujus energemate circumventus, quas ab ea didicit phaneroseis scripsit. Adhuc in saeculo supersunt qui meminerint eorum, etiam proprii discentes et successores ipsorum, ne se posteriores negare possint. Quanquam et de operibus suis, ut dixit Dominus, revincuntur. Si enim Marcion Novum Testamentum a Vetere separavit, posterior est eo quod separavit; quia separare non posset, nisi quod unitum fuit. Unitum ergo ante quam separaretur, postea separatum, posteriorem ostendit separatorem. Item Valentinus, aliter exponens, et sine dubio emendans, hoc omnino quicquid emendat, ut mendosum retro, anterius fuisse demonstrat. Hos ut insigniores et frequentiores adulteros veritatis nominamus. Caeterum et Nigidius nescio quis, et Hermogenes, et multi alii qui adhuc ambulant pervertentes vias Dei, ostendant mihi ex qua auctoritate prodierunt. Si alium Deum praedicant, quomodo ejus Dei rebus et litteris et nominibus utuntur adversus quem praedicant? si eumdem, quomodo aliter? Probent se novos apostolos esse: dicant Christum iterum descendisse, iterum ipsum docuisse, iterum crucifixum, iterum mortuum, iterum resuscitatum: sic enim Apostolos solet facere, dare illis praeterea virtutem eadem signa edendi, quae et ipse. Volo igitur et virtutes eorum proferri; nisi quod agnosco maximam virtutem eorum, qua Apostolos in perversum aemulantur: illi enim de mortuis vivos faciebant, isti de vivis mortuos faciunt.
pass_a_gloss: Where then was Marcion, the shipmaster from Pontus, a student of Stoic philosophy? Where was Valentinus, a follower of Platonic philosophy? For it is established that they were not even formerly, during the reign of Antoninus, and at first believed in the doctrine of the Catholic Church at Rome, under the episcopate of the blessed Eleutherius, until, because of their restless curiosity, by which they also avoided their brothers, having been ejected once and twice, Marcion was finally relegated to perpetual separation with the two hundred sestertii which he had brought to the Church, and they disseminated the poisons of their doctrines. Afterwards, the same Marcion, having confessed repentance when the condition given to him occurred, was going to receive peace if he restored to the Church the others whom he had instructed for destruction, but he was prevented by death. For it was necessary that there be heresies. Nor, however, are heresies good because it was necessary that they be, as if evil was not also necessary to be. For it was also necessary that the Lord be betrayed; but woe to the betrayer, lest someone also defend heresies from this. If even the lineage of Apelles is to be withdrawn, as much not old as Marcion himself, the founder and prefigurer of it: but having fallen into a woman, a deserter of Marcionite continence, he withdrew from the eyes of the most holy master Alexander to Alexandria; and from there, after years, having returned not better, except that he was no longer a Marcionite, he stumbled into another woman, that virgin Philumene, whom we mentioned above, and afterwards a monstrous prostitute, and he, having been deceived by her energy, wrote the revelations which he learned from her. There are still in the world those who remember them, even their own disciples and successors, so that they may not be able to deny themselves as posteriors. Although they are also overcome by their own works, as the Lord said. For if Marcion separated the New Testament from the Old, he is posterior to that which he separated; because he could not separate what was not united. Therefore, what was united before it was separated, afterwards separated, shows the separator to be posterior. Likewise, Valentinus, expounding otherwise and undoubtedly correcting, demonstrates that whatever he corrects was previously erroneous. We name these men as the most notable and frequent adulterers of the truth. Moreover, I ask Nigidius, whoever he is, and Hermogenes, and many others who still walk, perverting the ways of God, to show me from what authority they have come forth. If they preach another God, how do they use the things and letters and names of that God against whom they preach? If they preach the same God, how do they do so otherwise? Let them prove themselves to be new apostles: let them say that Christ descended again, taught again, was crucified again, died again, and was resurrected again: for thus the Apostles are accustomed to act, giving them also the power to produce the same signs which He Himself produces. I wish, therefore, their powers to be brought forth; unless I recognize that their greatest power, by which they emulate the Apostles perversely, is that they make the living dead, whereas the Apostles made the dead living.

choices.english: withdrew from the eyes of Alexander to Alexandria

pass_b_english: Where was Marcion then, the Pontic shipowner and Stoic enthusiast? Where was Valentinus, the Platonist disciple? The record shows they were not around even earlier, back under Antoninus; at first they actually believed the catholic teaching in the Roman church, under Bishop Eleutherius. But their restless curiosity — the kind that made even fellow Christians avoid them — got them thrown out once, then twice. Finally Marcion was cut off for good, taking his two hundred sestertii with him, and the pair scattered the poison of their doctrines. Later Marcion confessed repentance and tried to meet the condition set for his return: he would be readmitted only if he brought back to the church the others he had schooled for destruction. Death beat him to it. Heresies had to exist, yes; but that does not make heresies good, as if evil were not also necessary. The Lord had to be betrayed; still, woe to the betrayer — lest anyone use that as a defense of heresy. Even Apelles' pedigree needs examining: he is no more ancient than Marcion, his founder and forerunner. He fell for a woman, abandoned Marcionite continence, and slipped away from the eyes of the most holy teacher Alexander to Alexandria. Years later he came back no better, except that he was no longer a Marcionite; he stumbled into another woman, the virgin Philumene (mentioned above), who later became a monstrous prostitute. Deceived by her power, he wrote down the revelations he learned from her. People still alive remember them — their own disciples and successors — so they cannot deny being later arrivals. Though they are also refuted by their own works, as the Lord said. If Marcion split the New Testament from the Old, he comes after what he split; he could not split what was not already united. United first, then separated — that proves the splitter is later. Valentinus, explaining differently and 'correcting,' only shows that whatever he corrects was previously flawed. These are the most notorious and frequent adulterers of the truth. And what about Nigidius, whoever he is, and Hermogenes, and the rest still walking around perverting God's ways? Let them show me their authorization. If they preach another God, how do they use that God's own things, letters, and names against the God they preach? If they preach the same God, how do they do it differently? Let them prove they are new apostles: let them say Christ descended again, taught again, was crucified again, died again, rose again — because that is how apostles operate, receiving power to work the same signs he did. I want to see their powers produced; unless I acknowledge their greatest power, by which they perversely imitate the apostles: the apostles made the dead live; these men make the living dead.

review.notes: All clauses in the Latin source were checked against Pass A and Pass B. The translation preserves the nuances of the argument regarding Marcion's separation of the testaments and the comparison between the Apostles and heretics. Scripture references (implied by 'as the Lord said') are handled correctly in the context of the translation. No omissions or contradictions found.
